questions.stem: In a patient with right-sided infective endocarditis, this chest imaging shows multiple bilateral peripheral nodular lung lesions. What are they?

explanation.summary: Tricuspid valve vegetations shed infected fragments into the pulmonary circulation, producing multiple peripheral septic emboli that may cavitate. Their embolic, peripheral distribution and clinical context distinguish them from metastases or granulomatous disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tricuspid valve vegetations shed infected fragments into the pulmonary circulation, producing multiple peripheral septic emboli that may cavitate. Their embolic, peripheral distribution and clinical context distinguish them from metastases or granulomatous disease.

questions.stem: This lumbar spine MRI (circled) in a patient with endocarditis and new back pain shows a destructive disc and adjacent endplate lesion. What complication does this represent?

explanation.summary: Hematogenous seeding from endocarditis can infect the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae, producing pyogenic discitis-osteomyelitis. Disc-centered destruction with endplate involvement distinguishes it from the non-infectious distractors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematogenous seeding from endocarditis can infect the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae, producing pyogenic discitis-osteomyelitis. Disc-centered destruction with endplate involvement distinguishes it from the non-infectious distractors.

questions.stem: This fundus photograph in a patient with endocarditis shows retinal hemorrhages that have a pale center. What does that pale center chiefly consist of?

explanation.summary: The white center of a retinal hemorrhage in endocarditis is composed of fibrin, platelets, and inflammatory cells, marking it as an embolic/immunologic lesion rather than a lipid or pigmented deposit.
explanation.whyCorrect: The white center of a retinal hemorrhage in endocarditis is composed of fibrin, platelets, and inflammatory cells, marking it as an embolic/immunologic lesion rather than a lipid or pigmented deposit.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram shows a mobile mass attached to a heart valve (arrow) in suspected endocarditis. Which imaging test is the most sensitive gold standard for detecting this lesion?

explanation.summary: Transesophageal echocardiography provides the highest sensitivity for valvular vegetations because the probe sits directly behind the heart, avoiding chest-wall attenuation. It is the diagnostic standard when transthoracic imaging is inconclusive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transesophageal echocardiography provides the highest sensitivity for valvular vegetations because the probe sits directly behind the heart, avoiding chest-wall attenuation. It is the diagnostic standard when transthoracic imaging is inconclusive.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram shows a mobile echogenic mass attached to the tricuspid valve at the right atrial-right ventricular junction. In an afebrile-to-febrile patient, what is the classic risk factor for a vegetation in this location?

explanation.summary: Right-sided (tricuspid) endocarditis is strongly associated with intravenous drug use, as injected material and skin flora are delivered first to the right heart. It classically embolizes to the lungs rather than the systemic circulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Right-sided (tricuspid) endocarditis is strongly associated with intravenous drug use, as injected material and skin flora are delivered first to the right heart. It classically embolizes to the lungs rather than the systemic circulation.

questions.stem: The tender nodular lesions indicated on the finger pads are a peripheral stigma of infective endocarditis. What mechanism is classically responsible?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct bacterial invasion of the epidermis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Septic microemboli lodging in dermal vessels

explanation.summary: These tender lesions are attributed to immune-complex mediated vasculitis, which accounts for their pain. This contrasts with the painless palmar/plantar lesions that arise from septic emboli.
explanation.whyCorrect: These tender lesions are attributed to immune-complex mediated vasculitis, which accounts for their pain. This contrasts with the painless palmar/plantar lesions that arise from septic emboli.

questions.stem: The non-tender hemorrhagic macule on the palm indicated here is a peripheral sign of endocarditis. What mechanism produces it?

explanation.summary: These painless palmar/plantar macules result from septic emboli seeding small dermal vessels. Their painlessness and embolic origin distinguish them from the tender, immune-complex lesions of the finger pads.
explanation.whyCorrect: These painless palmar/plantar macules result from septic emboli seeding small dermal vessels. Their painlessness and embolic origin distinguish them from the tender, immune-complex lesions of the finger pads.

questions.stem: This close-up of a fingernail shows thin, longitudinal reddish-brown streaks beneath the nail plate in a patient with fever and a new murmur. What are these?

explanation.summary: Splinter hemorrhages are linear subungual microhemorrhages from embolic or vascular damage and are a recognized peripheral sign of infective endocarditis. Their thin linear form along the nail axis distinguishes them from pigmented or structural nail lesions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Splinter hemorrhages are linear subungual microhemorrhages from embolic or vascular damage and are a recognized peripheral sign of infective endocarditis. Their thin linear form along the nail axis distinguishes them from pigmented or structural nail lesions.

questions.stem: This gross specimen of an opened heart shows bulky, friable masses on the atrioventricular valve leaflets, formed by platelets, fibrin, and microorganisms deposited at sites of endothelial injury. What is the most common complication of these left-sided lesions?

explanation.summary: The masses are vegetations of infective endocarditis. Left-sided vegetations can break off and travel through the systemic circulation, producing septic emboli to the brain, kidneys, spleen, and extremities.
explanation.whyCorrect: The masses are vegetations of infective endocarditis. Left-sided vegetations can break off and travel through the systemic circulation, producing septic emboli to the brain, kidneys, spleen, and extremities.

questions.stem: This gross specimen shows small, bland thrombotic vegetations along the closure lines of the aortic valve leaflets, without underlying valve destruction. What is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Libman-Sacks endocarditis of the mitral valve

explanation.summary: Small, sterile, loosely attached vegetations on the valve closure lines without inflammation or leaflet destruction indicate nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis, associated with hypercoagulable/malignant states.
explanation.whyCorrect: Small, sterile, loosely attached vegetations on the valve closure lines without inflammation or leaflet destruction indicate nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis, associated with hypercoagulable/malignant states.

questions.stem: This gross specimen of an atrioventricular valve shows small nodular masses along the leaflet closure lines with intact underlying chordae and leaflet architecture. In a patient with advanced adenocarcinoma, these lesions most characteristically cause which complication?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chordae tendineae rupture with flail leaflet

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progressive valve leaflet perforation and acute regurgitation

explanation.summary: The bland, sterile fibrin-platelet vegetations of nonbacterial thrombotic (marantic) endocarditis form on the valve without tissue destruction and readily embolize, producing infarcts in the brain and other organs; they are classically associated with hypercoagulable states such as mucinous adenocarcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bland, sterile fibrin-platelet vegetations of nonbacterial thrombotic (marantic) endocarditis form on the valve without tissue destruction and readily embolize, producing infarcts in the brain and other organs; they are classically associated with hypercoagulable states such as mucinous adenocarcinoma.

questions.stem: These three schematics contrast vegetation patterns on a valve leaflet. Which entity is characterized by small, sterile verrucous vegetations distributed on BOTH surfaces of the leaflet, typically in systemic lupus erythematosus?

explanation.summary: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) produces small sterile vegetations on both the atrial and ventricular surfaces of the valve, unlike the large friable single-surface masses of infective endocarditis or the small along-the-line-of-closure vegetations of marantic endocarditis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) produces small sterile vegetations on both the atrial and ventricular surfaces of the valve, unlike the large friable single-surface masses of infective endocarditis or the small along-the-line-of-closure vegetations of marantic endocarditis.

questions.stem: This diagram illustrates the layered wrapping around the heart. Because the outer fibrous layer is tough and poorly distensible, rapid filling of the space between the serous layers produces which acute complication?

explanation.summary: The non-compliant fibrous pericardium cannot accommodate rapidly accumulating fluid, so intrapericardial pressure rises and compresses the heart, producing tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: The non-compliant fibrous pericardium cannot accommodate rapidly accumulating fluid, so intrapericardial pressure rises and compresses the heart, producing tamponade.

questions.stem: This is a normal histologic section taken from the outer surface of the heart. The thin mesothelial lining at the labeled surface normally performs which function?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Filters lymph before it enters the thoracic duct

explanation.summary: The visceral pericardium (epicardium) is lined by mesothelium that secretes a small amount of serous fluid, allowing frictionless movement of the heart within the pericardial sac.
explanation.whyCorrect: The visceral pericardium (epicardium) is lined by mesothelium that secretes a small amount of serous fluid, allowing frictionless movement of the heart within the pericardial sac.

questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG shows diffuse concave ST-segment elevation across multiple leads together with PR-segment depression. Which diagnosis do these findings most strongly suggest?

explanation.summary: Diffuse (non-territorial) concave ST elevation with PR depression, typically sparing aVR, is characteristic of acute pericarditis rather than the regional ST elevation of an infarct.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diffuse (non-territorial) concave ST elevation with PR depression, typically sparing aVR, is characteristic of acute pericarditis rather than the regional ST elevation of an infarct.

questions.stem: This axial CT of the chest shows a large fluid collection surrounding the heart within the pericardial sac. If this fluid accumulates rapidly, what is the most immediately life-threatening consequence?

explanation.summary: Rapid accumulation of pericardial fluid raises intrapericardial pressure faster than the fibrous pericardium can stretch, compressing the chambers and impairing diastolic filling — cardiac tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rapid accumulation of pericardial fluid raises intrapericardial pressure faster than the fibrous pericardium can stretch, compressing the chambers and impairing diastolic filling — cardiac tamponade.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a needle being advanced at roughly 45 degrees just below the xiphoid toward the fluid-filled sac around the heart. What procedure is being depicted?

explanation.summary: A needle inserted from a subxiphoid position at ~45 degrees to aspirate fluid from the pericardial sac defines pericardiocentesis, the emergency treatment for cardiac tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: A needle inserted from a subxiphoid position at ~45 degrees to aspirate fluid from the pericardial sac defines pericardiocentesis, the emergency treatment for cardiac tamponade.

questions.stem: This section of pericardium shows a thickened, inflamed surface coated by eosinophilic strands of fibrin. This appearance is the hallmark of which type of pericarditis?

explanation.summary: Fibrin deposition over an inflamed, thickened pericardial surface — the most common pattern in acute pericarditis — defines fibrinous pericarditis and underlies the auscultated friction rub.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fibrin deposition over an inflamed, thickened pericardial surface — the most common pattern in acute pericarditis — defines fibrinous pericarditis and underlies the auscultated friction rub.

questions.stem: This heart, lifted at autopsy, has a shaggy, roughened epicardial surface covered by a thick fibrinous exudate (a 'bread-and-butter' appearance). What is the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: The shaggy 'bread-and-butter' epicardial exudate of fibrin is the classic gross appearance of fibrinous pericarditis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The shaggy 'bread-and-butter' epicardial exudate of fibrin is the classic gross appearance of fibrinous pericarditis.

questions.stem: This pericardial section is filled with a dense infiltrate of neutrophils forming purulent fluid. Which underlying cause is most consistent with this pattern?

explanation.summary: A neutrophil-rich, purulent exudate indicates suppurative (bacterial) pericarditis, typically from direct spread or hematogenous seeding of pyogenic organisms.
explanation.whyCorrect: A neutrophil-rich, purulent exudate indicates suppurative (bacterial) pericarditis, typically from direct spread or hematogenous seeding of pyogenic organisms.

questions.stem: This tracing aligns arterial blood pressure with respiration and shows an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic pressure. In a patient with this finding, what is the most likely underlying condition?

explanation.summary: The tracing shows pulsus paradoxus, an inspiratory drop in systolic pressure exceeding 10 mmHg. It classically indicates cardiac tamponade (and also severe asthma or constrictive physiology), where inspiratory augmentation of RV filling compresses the LV and reduces stroke volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tracing shows pulsus paradoxus, an inspiratory drop in systolic pressure exceeding 10 mmHg. It classically indicates cardiac tamponade (and also severe asthma or constrictive physiology), where inspiratory augmentation of RV filling compresses the LV and reduces stroke volume.

questions.stem: On this chest radiograph, the arrows outline a thin curvilinear density surrounding the cardiac silhouette. In the setting of constrictive pericarditis, what does this finding represent?

explanation.summary: A rim of calcification tracing the cardiac border is a classic radiographic clue to chronic constrictive pericarditis, reflecting long-standing pericardial inflammation and fibrocalcific thickening.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rim of calcification tracing the cardiac border is a classic radiographic clue to chronic constrictive pericarditis, reflecting long-standing pericardial inflammation and fibrocalcific thickening.

questions.stem: The insets contrast a normal pericardium with the result after the outlined structure is surgically removed. In constrictive pericarditis, why is removing this layer therapeutic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It drains an infected pleural effusion compressing the lung

choices.label: B
choices.text: It eliminates the rigid, thickened sac that restricts diastolic filling

choices.label: C
choices.text: It relieves coronary artery obstruction limiting myocardial perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: It repairs an incompetent valve causing regurgitation

choices.label: E
choices.text: It resects hypertrophied myocardium obstructing outflow

explanation.summary: In constrictive pericarditis the fibrotic, rigid pericardium encases the heart and prevents adequate diastolic filling; pericardiectomy (removal of the pericardium) frees the ventricles to fill normally, relieving the constriction.
explanation.whyCorrect: In constrictive pericarditis the fibrotic, rigid pericardium encases the heart and prevents adequate diastolic filling; pericardiectomy (removal of the pericardium) frees the ventricles to fill normally, relieving the constriction.

questions.stem: This tracing shows left and right ventricular volumes across the respiratory cycle in constrictive pericarditis, with the two ventricles filling reciprocally. What phenomenon does this illustrate?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Left bundle branch block delaying LV contraction

explanation.summary: A rigid pericardium fixes total cardiac volume, so inspiratory increases in right ventricular filling occur at the expense of left ventricular filling (and the reverse on expiration); this exaggerated ventricular interdependence underlies the discordant volume changes and the respiratory variation seen in constriction.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rigid pericardium fixes total cardiac volume, so inspiratory increases in right ventricular filling occur at the expense of left ventricular filling (and the reverse on expiration); this exaggerated ventricular interdependence underlies the discordant volume changes and the respiratory variation seen in constriction.

questions.stem: These paired heart-and-circulation diagrams (normal, distributive, cardiogenic, hypovolemic, neurogenic, obstructive) are organized to convey what?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The types of congestive heart failure

explanation.summary: Each panel contrasts blood flow and volume against a normal circulation to illustrate how the major categories of shock differ in their underlying hemodynamic derangement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each panel contrasts blood flow and volume against a normal circulation to illustrate how the major categories of shock differ in their underlying hemodynamic derangement.

questions.stem: This hemodynamic graph shows cardiac output rising well above normal while both preload and afterload fall below normal. Which category of shock does this pattern represent?

explanation.summary: Widespread vasodilation lowers systemic vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload), while a compensatory high cardiac output produces the warm, hyperdynamic profile typical of early distributive/septic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Widespread vasodilation lowers systemic vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload), while a compensatory high cardiac output produces the warm, hyperdynamic profile typical of early distributive/septic shock.

questions.stem: This graph shows preload and afterload both increased while cardiac output is markedly decreased. Which category of shock does this represent?

explanation.summary: Pump failure lowers cardiac output while blood backs up (raising preload) and compensatory vasoconstriction raises afterload, the hallmark pattern of cardiogenic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pump failure lowers cardiac output while blood backs up (raising preload) and compensatory vasoconstriction raises afterload, the hallmark pattern of cardiogenic shock.

questions.stem: This graph shows afterload increased while preload and cardiac output are both decreased. Which category of shock does this represent?

explanation.summary: Loss of intravascular volume drops venous return (preload) and cardiac output, while compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction raises afterload, characteristic of hypovolemic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of intravascular volume drops venous return (preload) and cardiac output, while compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction raises afterload, characteristic of hypovolemic shock.

questions.stem: This graph shows preload, afterload, and cardiac output all decreased below normal. Which category of shock does this represent?

explanation.summary: Loss of sympathetic tone lowers vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload) without a compensatory rise in output, so cardiac output also falls, the pattern of neurogenic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of sympathetic tone lowers vascular resistance (afterload) and venous return (preload) without a compensatory rise in output, so cardiac output also falls, the pattern of neurogenic shock.

questions.stem: These paired graphs contrast right- and left-sided loading (e.g., raised RV preload but falling LV preload and cardiac output) depending on where flow is blocked. Which category of shock is depicted?

explanation.summary: A mechanical obstruction (e.g., pulmonary embolism or tamponade) impedes filling or ejection, so preload distributes unevenly across the ventricles while cardiac output falls, defining obstructive shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: A mechanical obstruction (e.g., pulmonary embolism or tamponade) impedes filling or ejection, so preload distributes unevenly across the ventricles while cardiac output falls, defining obstructive shock.

questions.stem: This figure shows a balloon-tipped catheter advanced through the right heart into a pulmonary artery branch, with characteristic RA, RV, PA, and wedge pressure waveforms. When the balloon is wedged, the measured pressure most closely estimates which value?

explanation.summary: With the balloon wedged, forward pulmonary artery flow is occluded and the catheter tip senses pressure transmitted back through the pulmonary capillary bed from the left atrium. The pulmonary artery wedge (occlusion) pressure therefore approximates left atrial pressure and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, a measure of left-heart preload.
explanation.whyCorrect: With the balloon wedged, forward pulmonary artery flow is occluded and the catheter tip senses pressure transmitted back through the pulmonary capillary bed from the left atrium. The pulmonary artery wedge (occlusion) pressure therefore approximates left atrial pressure and left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, a measure of left-heart preload.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph shows enlarged central pulmonary vessels, hazy interstitial markings extending toward the lung bases, and an enlarged cardiac silhouette. These findings are most consistent with which condition?

explanation.summary: Enlarged central pulmonary vessels (pulmonary venous congestion), interstitial edema, and cardiomegaly indicate raised left atrial/pulmonary venous pressure, i.e., cardiogenic pulmonary edema from left-heart failure. Pneumonia is typically focal/consolidative, pneumothorax shows lucency with lung collapse, and fibrosis/emphysema have distinct chronic patterns.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enlarged central pulmonary vessels (pulmonary venous congestion), interstitial edema, and cardiomegaly indicate raised left atrial/pulmonary venous pressure, i.e., cardiogenic pulmonary edema from left-heart failure. Pneumonia is typically focal/consolidative, pneumothorax shows lucency with lung collapse, and fibrosis/emphysema have distinct chronic patterns.

questions.stem: This signaling diagram shows dobutamine acting via beta-1/Gs/adenylyl cyclase to raise cAMP, while a second drug blocks PDE3; both converge on increased intracellular Ca2+ and contractility. By what mechanism does the PDE3-blocking drug (milrinone) increase contractility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase like a cardiac glycoside

choices.label: B
choices.text: It inhibits phosphodiesterase-3, preventing cAMP breakdown

choices.label: C
choices.text: It opens L-type calcium channels directly

choices.label: D
choices.text: It directly stimulates the beta-1 adrenergic receptor

choices.label: E
choices.text: It increases nitric oxide production in the myocyte

explanation.summary: Milrinone inhibits PDE3, the enzyme that degrades cAMP. With cAMP breakdown blocked, intracellular cAMP accumulates, raising Ca2+ and augmenting contractility, an inotropic effect that does not require the beta-receptor (unlike dobutamine, which works upstream through beta-1/Gs/adenylyl cyclase).
explanation.whyCorrect: Milrinone inhibits PDE3, the enzyme that degrades cAMP. With cAMP breakdown blocked, intracellular cAMP accumulates, raising Ca2+ and augmenting contractility, an inotropic effect that does not require the beta-receptor (unlike dobutamine, which works upstream through beta-1/Gs/adenylyl cyclase).

questions.stem: These paired illustrations show a device positioned in the descending aorta that is expanded during diastole and collapsed during systole. What is this therapeutic device?

explanation.summary: The intra-aortic balloon pump inflates in diastole (augmenting coronary perfusion pressure) and deflates just before systole (reducing afterload), improving myocardial oxygen supply and cardiac output. This counterpulsation is used as mechanical support in cardiogenic shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: The intra-aortic balloon pump inflates in diastole (augmenting coronary perfusion pressure) and deflates just before systole (reducing afterload), improving myocardial oxygen supply and cardiac output. This counterpulsation is used as mechanical support in cardiogenic shock.

questions.stem: The magnified inset shows the layers surrounding the heart. Between which two layers does a pericardial effusion accumulate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Between the myocardium and the visceral pericardium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Between the visceral and parietal layers of serous pericardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Between the fibrous pericardium and the chest wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Between the endocardium and the myocardium

explanation.summary: The pericardial cavity lies between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal serous layers. Effusion fluid collects in this potential space; normally it holds only a small volume of lubricating fluid.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pericardial cavity lies between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal serous layers. Effusion fluid collects in this potential space; normally it holds only a small volume of lubricating fluid.

questions.stem: The echocardiogram and diagram show inward buckling of the right ventricular free wall during ventricular diastole. Why does this occur, and what does it signify?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The RV wall is hypertrophied and stiff from pulmonary hypertension

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intrapericardial pressure transiently exceeds RV filling pressure, an early sign of cardiac tamponade

choices.label: C
choices.text: A large myocardial infarction has scarred the RV free wall

choices.label: D
choices.text: The RV is dilating because of a left-to-right shunt

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tricuspid regurgitation is overloading the right ventricle

explanation.summary: In tamponade the lowest-pressure chambers collapse first. During diastole, when RV pressure is lowest, rising pericardial pressure exceeds it and buckles the RV free wall inward, an early echocardiographic marker.
explanation.whyCorrect: In tamponade the lowest-pressure chambers collapse first. During diastole, when RV pressure is lowest, rising pericardial pressure exceeds it and buckles the RV free wall inward, an early echocardiographic marker.

explanation.summary: Beck triad, distended neck veins, distant/muffled heart sounds, and decreased blood pressure, reflects impaired cardiac filling and low output in acute cardiac tamponade.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beck triad, distended neck veins, distant/muffled heart sounds, and decreased blood pressure, reflects impaired cardiac filling and low output in acute cardiac tamponade.

questions.stem: Comparing the normal heart with the tamponade panel, why do the RA and RV appear compressed and reduced in size?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The right chambers hypertrophy and thicken, shrinking their cavities

choices.label: B
choices.text: The aortic arch dilates and mechanically displaces the right chambers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapid tachycardia empties the right chambers of blood

choices.label: D

choices.label: E
choices.text: Accumulated pericardial fluid raises pressure that compresses the low-pressure right chambers
